The change is ready for your merge approval. The critic passed it in round 1 of 4, after 4 of the 10 allowed dispatches.

**Round 0.** The builder added `parseRanges`, its tests and a README section, and `npm test` passed. The critic still failed it: all 6 checklist items held, but 18 of the 70 held-out cases failed. On five open questions the builder had made the opposite choice to the hidden suite:
- it sorted the result instead of keeping the typed order;
- it merged repeated pages instead of keeping them;
- it rejected backward ranges like `"5-3"` instead of counting down;
- it rejected open ranges like `"8-"` and `"-3"` instead of running to the last or first page;
- it rejected empty text instead of returning every page.

**Round 1.** A fresh builder got only REVIEW.md and changed the code, tests, README and CHANGES.md to match those 18 cases. A fresh critic then judged the change from scratch:
- all 6 checklist items hold, each cited with file and line;
- all 70 held-out cases pass;
- `npm test` passes 16 of 16, with none skipped.

**Choices the suite left open, so the critic never tested them:**
- A lone `"-"` throws a RangeError.
- An open range with an end outside the document (`"11-"`, `"-0"`) throws a RangeError.
- An empty part inside non-empty text (`"1,"`, `"1,,3"`) throws a RangeError, although blank text as a whole means every page.

**In the working tree, not committed:**
- `src/parse-ranges.mjs`, new
- `tests/parse-ranges.test.mjs`, new
- `README.md`, a new section
- `CHANGES.md`, new
- `REVIEW.md`, new

Nothing is committed yet. CHANGES.md and REVIEW.md are records of the review loop, so you may not want them in the merge.

**Merge it?** If you approve, I'll end the run as a success; I can also commit the change on a new branch if you want that. If you reject it, give me your feedback and I'll send it to the builder for another round.
